name: Scion Asset Management
blurb: The 'Big Short' investor. Tiny, contrarian, often hedged book with sharp, concentrated convictions.
status_note: Michael Burry deregistered Scion Asset Management with the SEC; its registration shows as terminated. In a letter to investors dated 27 October 2025 he said he would liquidate the funds and return capital by year-end, writing that his estimation of value in securities had not been in sync with the markets for some time. The holdings below are the last 13F Scion filed and are not a live book. He did not stop investing, though — since November 2025 he has published Cassandra Unchained on Substack, and since late July 2026 a near-daily 'Trading Post' describing his own buys, shorts and options. That is more current than a 13F ever was, and covers shorts and options a 13F never showed, but it is paid and not machine-readable: this app can see that he wrote and when, never what he holds.

profile.background: Michael Burry trained as a physician — Vanderbilt MD, neurology residency at Stanford — and wrote about stocks at night on message boards until the readership became a fund. He has spoken publicly about being diagnosed with Asperger's.
profile.approach: Deep value with a contrarian bias, run as a very small and highly concentrated book — essentially friends and family money rather than a marketed fund — and frequently expressed through options rather than shares. Positions were often macro theses wearing an equity ticker.
profile.known_for: Buying credit default swaps against subprime mortgage bonds from 2005, the trade at the centre of Michael Lewis's The Big Short. Scion was deregistered in November 2025 and no longer operates as a hedge fund; see the status note above for the reporting.
